narratives.Description: bug(doctor,setup): existing root check can stay green without Directive, and setup still says task check
narratives.Overview:
1. On the include-ok path, when a root task named check exists and does not invoke Directive's check, record a warning finding and do not emit Gates-surface ready. Leave the process exit at 0. Do not write the file, including through the fixMode yes branch. Emit Gates-surface ready only when that root check task is absent, or when it invokes Directive's check.
2. Count invocation only as command-position deft check or directive check that is not failure-masked; command-position task deft:check, task deft:check:consumer, or task deft:check:framework-source as the whole task token; a go-task cmds or deps entry whose task name is one of those three; or engine:invoke paired with ENGINE_CMD check when that task is the dispatcher the deft include deposits. A consumer-owned task of the same name does not count. Do not count bare task check, task check followed by some other suffix, comments, echo, or a masked status. Keep stripTaskBodyComments. Read the file resolveConsumerTaskfile already selected. Do not call evaluateConsumerCheckContract for this warning.
3. Write the Quality clause as the prefer/else sentence already in agents-entry: prefer deft check, else task deft:check on an include-only consumer, one gate, not two runs. Keep the coverage clause and the secrets clause. Use that same pair on the setup-copied pull-request checklist item. Do not add a root check task to MINIMAL_TASKFILE. Rebuild the skills pack from the skill when the sentence changes. Leave the framework-repo skip in place.

audit-targets: none

The refutation target survives. Doctor should warn, and should not rewrite the file, when a root check task exists and does not invoke Directive's check. The setup Quality sentence should name deft check and task deft:check for an include-only consumer. Both halves match c7cae4d44e40abf4fb00ee25aceacf32d06168d9. The statement has to get tighter before bind, in the three places below.

## Withholding the ready line
sharpens-framing
Evidence: git show c7cae4d44e40abf4fb00ee25aceacf32d06168d9:packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts. runTaskfileIncludeCheck, on include status ok, calls sink.success with "Gates-surface ready: root Taskfile.yml includes the deft framework (`task deft:<verb>`)" and returns. It does not read a task body. classifyTaskfileInclude in packages/core/src/doctor/taskfile.ts returns ok when the includes block points at a .deft/core or legacy deft Taskfile. Findings with severity warning do not increment errorCount. exitCode is 1 only when errorCount is greater than 0. Plain output prints "System check passed!" only when errorCount and warningCount are both 0. A warning finding instead ends on "System check completed with N warning(s)." and still returns 0. JSON ok follows that exit code.
Failure mode: A warning printed beside the ready success still tells the operator the include is the gate. That ready line is the recorded pain. Skipping addFinding leaves warningCount at 0, so the footer still says the system check passed. Reusing the missing-file branch, which writes a Taskfile when fixMode, a tty, and a yes answer are all set, would rewrite an existing consumer Taskfile.
Disposition: On the include-ok path, when a root task named check exists and does not invoke Directive's check, record a warning finding and do not emit Gates-surface ready. Leave the process exit at 0. Do not write the file, including through that fixMode yes branch. Emit Gates-surface ready only when that root check task is absent, or when it invokes Directive's check.

## Which command counts as invoke
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Imported taskBodyInvokesCheckOrchestrator and runCommandIsFullCheck from packages/core/src/consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts at this SHA (Node strip-types, .js specifiers resolved to the sibling .ts files) and ran them on task bodies. Shell "deft check", "directive check", and "task deft:check" return true. Shell "task check" and "task check:lint" return true. Go-task "task: deft:check", a deps list of deft:check, a deps entry "task: deft:check", and "task: deft:check:consumer" return false. A comment line, "echo run deft check", and "deft check || true" return false. The framework Taskfile.yml check body, engine:invoke paired with ENGINE_CMD check, returns true. Separately, task.exe in a temp directory: an include-only Taskfile and `task check --dry` exited 200 with Task "check" does not exist. The same file plus a root check whose command is echo consumer-only exited 0.
Failure mode: Using taskBodyInvokesCheckOrchestrator unchanged stays silent when the root check runs `task check:lint` or bare `task check`, so task check stays green and the ready line still describes the include. The same function warns when the root check delegates with go-task task: deft:check or a deps entry deft:check, which does run Directive. A raw text search would let a comment that contains deft check suppress the warning. The Taskfile is untrusted local input, and comment text must not decide the ready result. evaluateConsumerCheckContract is the wrong caller for this warning. It trusts an orchestrator body only when project-root tasks/verify.yml defines every required gate, so a consumer check command of deft check still fails that contract, and it reads only Taskfile.yml while resolveConsumerTaskfile also accepts Taskfile.yaml.
Disposition: Count invocation only as command-position deft check or directive check that is not failure-masked; command-position task deft:check, task deft:check:consumer, or task deft:check:framework-source as the whole task token; a go-task cmds or deps entry whose task name is one of those three; or engine:invoke paired with ENGINE_CMD check. Do not count bare task check, task check followed by some other suffix, comments, echo, or a masked status. Keep stripTaskBodyComments. Read the file resolveConsumerTaskfile already selected. Do not call evaluateConsumerCheckContract for this warning. Calling that contract from doctor was the rejected alternative: it already fails a partial root check, and the include must not hide those gaps, but it does not run when the operator types only their own task check, and it false-fails a real deft check delegation unless root tasks/verify.yml is present. What would flip that rejection is an acceptance that doctor errors, and that trust includes the deposited .deft/core tasks/verify.yml. This target is a warning that does not rewrite the file.

## Quality sentence and the copied checklist
sharpens-framing
Evidence: git show c7cae4d44e40abf4fb00ee25aceacf32d06168d9:content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md. The Phase 2 template Quality string is "Run task check before every commit. Achieve >= {coverage}% coverage overall + per-module. Store secrets in secrets/ dir." The same skill's process-only pointer already names deft check. The same skill copies templates/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md into the consumer when the operator accepts, and does not overwrite an existing file. That template checklist item says task check passes locally (content/templates/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). content/templates/agents-entry.md says prefer deft check, else task deft:check on include-only consumers, one gate, not two runs. packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts MINIMAL_TASKFILE already says prefer deft check first, then task deft:check on this include-only consumer, and do not add a root check alias. That file has no tasks section.
Failure mode: Replacing the words task check inside the existing "Run ... before every commit" sentence produces a Quality narrative that tells every new project to run deft check and task deft:check. That fights the one-gate line already shipped in agents-entry. The copied checklist still tells a consumer who accepts the scaffold to run task check, which is the command that exited 200 on the include-only Taskfile above.
Disposition: Write the Quality clause as the prefer/else sentence already in agents-entry: prefer deft check, else task deft:check on an include-only consumer, one gate, not two runs. Keep the coverage clause and the secrets clause. Use that same pair on the setup-copied pull-request checklist item. Do not add a root check task to MINIMAL_TASKFILE.

## Adjacent mentions
footnote
Evidence: The same setup skill mentions task check when it describes a coverage omit for a display-bound GUI, and again in a historical note about project:export-spec. content/docs/getting-started.md already names deft check as the journey verb and task deft:check as the include-only form of the same gate. content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json embeds the skill body and is rebuilt from SKILL.md. runTaskfileIncludeCheck returns before the include read when runningInsideDeftRepo is true. The framework check task already invokes Directive, as the probe above showed.
Failure mode: None of these decide the warning or the Quality sentence. A pack drift failure is the existing rebuild. The framework-repo skip stays correct because that repo's own check task is the Directive gate.
Disposition: No change to the target. Rebuild the skills pack from the skill when the sentence changes. Leave the framework-repo skip in place.

## P1: a consumer-owned engine task satisfies the allowed pattern without running Directive
blocks-the-design

Evidence: Bound-remedy item 2 expressly counts `engine:invoke` paired with `ENGINE_CMD check`. At the pinned SHA, `packages/core/src/consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts` likewise recognizes those two syntactic markers without resolving the invoked task. The framework's own `Taskfile.yml` uses this pair, but doctor skips that framework repository. In a consumer root, an unqualified `engine:invoke` can name a consumer-owned task; its name is not evidence that it invokes Directive.

I ran `task --dir <temporary-directory> check` against this Taskfile:

```yaml
version: '3'
includes:
  deft:
    taskfile: ./.deft/core/Taskfile.yml
    optional: true
tasks:
  check:
    cmds:
      - task: engine:invoke
        vars:
          ENGINE_CMD: check
  engine:invoke:
    cmds:
      - echo consumer-only
```

Observed output: `task: [engine:invoke] echo consumer-only`, then `consumer-only`; exit 0. Directive's check never runs. This is an execution measurement, not a measurement of an unimplemented doctor change. The proposed rule's result follows from its explicit accepted pair.

The pinned `packages/core/src/doctor/taskfile.ts` classifies this include as `ok` from the include text, without requiring the optional target file to exist. That is not essential to the counterexample: installing the namespaced deft include does not change what this root-owned, unqualified task executes. The pinned `runTaskfileIncludeCheck` currently emits the ready line immediately for include-ok; item 1 of the remedy preserves that line for invocations accepted by item 2.

Failure mode: an ordinary consumer task name and variable become authority for the ready result even though the actual command only echoes text. No malicious comment or shell failure masking is needed. Thus the exact P1 outcome remains permitted by the remedy.

Disposition consequence: the P1 relief assertion does not hold as written, so this harvest cannot bind unchanged. The engine-pair exception needs evidence that its target actually delegates to Directive, or must not grant readiness for a consumer-owned target. This does not require changing the warning-only posture or adding a root alias. The strongest case for retaining the exception is compatibility with the real framework dispatcher; that case does not establish the identity of a consumer-local task. A contract restriction that excludes this executable counterexample would change this verdict.

## P2: the new-consumer instructions point to an available gate
footnote

I independently reproduced exit 200 for `task check` using the same temporary include-only Taskfile before adding its tasks section. Pinned `scaffold.ts` supplies that include-only shape without a root check. The pinned setup skill writes the bare `task check` Quality sentence and copies `content/templates/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, whose checklist also names bare `task check`.

Bound-remedy item 3 changes both instruction sources to the existing prefer/else command pair, explicitly requires one gate rather than two runs, preserves coverage and secrets clauses, and rebuilds the skills pack. It leaves the include-only Taskfile intact. This covers the named new-consumer pain; no P2 harvest change is needed. This assessment concerns the proposed contract, not a claim that the implementation has shipped.

## P1: the revised dispatcher restriction removes the prior counterexample
footnote

Pinned packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts currently returns success immediately for include-ok. packages/core/src/doctor/taskfile.ts establishes that status from include text, not the root check body. The existing consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts helper accepts engine:invoke plus ENGINE_CMD check without resolving task identity; it cannot, unchanged, establish the revised restriction.

I independently ran a temporary Taskfile with a deft include, root check delegating to a consumer-owned engine:invoke, ENGINE_CMD: check, and that local task executing echo consumer-only. It printed consumer-only and exited 0. The new item 2 explicitly excludes that task: only the deposited Directive dispatcher qualifies for the engine-pair exception. Item 1 therefore requires a warning finding and suppresses Gates-surface ready for this case, while preserving exit 0 and prohibiting a file rewrite. The old failure no longer satisfies the proposed rule.

The authority distinction is substantive: a consumer-controlled task name and variable alone no longer certify Directive execution. Keeping comment stripping, rejecting echo and masked status, and selecting the file through resolveConsumerTaskfile support the same boundary. The framework-repository skip does not grant a consumer-owned dispatcher that identity.

As a separate namespace probe, a real temporary included Taskfile with an echo-only check stand-in was reached by task: deft:check. Attempting to shadow that name with a root-owned deft:check instead failed with duplicate-task exit 203; it did not silently run the shadow. This tests go-task resolution only, not the Directive gate itself. The pinned framework Taskfile's actual check delegates through engine:invoke with ENGINE_CMD check. No additional design mechanism is proposed, and no P1 harvest change is needed.

## In plain English

Doctor was reporting gates-surface ready from the deft include alone, so a root check that never runs Directive still looked fine. Setup was telling a new consumer to run task check, and that command exits 200 on a fresh include-only Taskfile.

The build contract is the bound list on the successor lean. Doctor withholds the ready line and records a warning when a root check task does not invoke Directive. The process still exits 0, and doctor does not write the file. The engine pair counts only when that task is the dispatcher the deft include deposits. A consumer-owned task of the same name does not count. The Quality sentence and the copied pull-request checklist say prefer deft check, else task deft:check on an include-only consumer, one gate.

design-critique: synthesis accepted, because agents agreed (empty disagreement set)

Bound contract: successor lean 5795154473.

## Verified-claims table

| Verified claim | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A consumer-owned engine:invoke that only echoes text, paired with ENGINE_CMD check, exits 0 | The bound rule does not count that task. Doctor records a warning and withholds the ready line |
| task check on an include-only Taskfile exits 200 | The Quality sentence and the copied checklist name deft check, else task deft:check, one gate |
| Human merge is not this issue | Doctor does not write the file, and a fresh include-only Taskfile still has no root check task |

metadata.issueBody:
### Problem

Two leftovers from #967. The three stories on that issue do not bind: a root check alias, a starter template, and a setup step that edits the consumer Taskfile. Closed #4379 already keeps root aliases out. deft check, then task deft:check, already runs Directive's check.

1. Brownfield silence. ensureTaskfile (packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts) inserts the deft include and leaves an existing root check task unchanged. runTaskfileIncludeCheck (packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts) reports "Gates-surface ready" when that include is present and does not read the root check body. task check can exit 0 without Directive.

2. Setup prose. content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md writes the Phase 2 Quality narrative as "Run task check before every commit.". On a fresh include-only Taskfile, task check is exit 200. The sentence should name deft check, then task deft:check on an include-only consumer.

### Out of scope

- Do not deposit a root check alias.
- Do not add a starter Taskfile template.
- Do not add a setup step that edits a consumer Taskfile.
- Do not unnamespace the include or reopen #4379 / #3218.

### Acceptance

- Doctor warns when a root check exists and does not invoke Directive's check. The warning does not rewrite the file.
- The setup Quality sentence names deft check, then task deft:check on an include-only consumer, instead of bare task check.
- A fresh include-only Taskfile still has no root check task.

Leftover of #967. Design-critique lean https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/967#issuecomment-5787797921. The three stories stay closed.
